INC-001.title: Payment API Database Connection Timeout
symptoms: Database connection pool saturated (50/50 sockets)
HTTP 503 Service Unavailable on /api/v1/payments
Payment callback queue backlog exceeded 15,000 tasks
Gateway timeout on payment webhook processing
investigation_steps: Checked Postgres active connections in pg_stat_activity
Inspected uvicorn worker pool memory and socket descriptors
Identified unclosed DB session in payment_webhook_callback handler
Verified database server CPU and IOPS were under 35%
findings: Database server itself was healthy and responsive
Application worker processes were failing to return connection handles to pool
Connection leak triggered whenever client disconnected prematurely during webhook processing
INC-001.root_cause: Worker process had a connection leak in async webhook callback handler (database sockets unreleased on client timeout/disconnect).
actions_taken: Gracefully restarted affected payment worker pods
Deployed hotfix v2.4.2 wrapping db_session in try-finally context manager
INC-001.resolution: Restarted affected worker processes and deployed connection-pool context manager fix in v2.4.2.
INC-001.verification: Error rate returned to 0.01%, active DB connections stabilized at 12/50 under full production load.
recommendations: Enforce connection pool timeout ceiling of 5 seconds in PgBouncer
Add automated alert for unclosed connection pool sockets > 80%
INC-001.engineer_feedback: Hotfix v2.4.2 stabilized the connection pool. Night shift should monitor connection counts during scheduled 22:00 batch.

INC-002.title: Payment API Database Overload via Unindexed Batch Query
symptoms: Postgres connection timeouts across all API clients
Database server CPU pegged at 98%
p99 latency spiked to 6.8s on primary read/write node
IOPS ceiling reached on primary storage volume
investigation_steps: Queried pg_stat_activity for longest running queries
Discovered full table scan query on 14M rows in ledger_transactions table
Confirmed application worker pool was NOT leaking sockets
Identified new reporting batch cron triggered on primary rather than read-replica
findings: Root cause is database engine CPU & I/O overload, NOT a connection leak in application code
Worker connection pool saturated because database server was unable to service queries fast enough
INC-002.root_cause: Database CPU and I/O overload caused by unindexed analytical reporting query executing against primary database replica.
actions_taken: Added composite index on ledger_transactions(merchant_id, created_at)
Redirected reporting-worker connection string to read-only replica endpoint
INC-002.resolution: Terminated blocking query, added index on ledger_transactions, and redirected analytical traffic to read replica.
INC-002.verification: Database CPU dropped from 98% to 18%, p99 latency returned to 45ms, and connection pool backlog cleared immediately.
recommendations: Enforce read-replica routing for all automated reporting and reconciliation queries
INC-002.engineer_feedback: Important distinction: Even though symptom was DB connection timeout, cause was DB server overload from batch query, not a worker leak.

INC-003.title: Checkout Gateway HTTP 504 Downstream Partner Timeout
symptoms: HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout on checkout payment submission endpoints
Upstream thread pool exhaustion on API Gateway
Customer checkout abandonment spike of 45%
investigation_steps: Analyzed distributed trace spans in OpenTelemetry collector
Identified 94% of latency spent in external HTTP call to third-party card processing partner
Confirmed internal application database and cache response times were normal (< 12ms)
Checked partner status dashboard and confirmed regional degradation
findings: Downstream card processor API was taking 14+ seconds per authorization request without failing fast
INC-003.root_cause: Downstream payment processing provider experienced regional latency degradation, exhausting local connection threads due to lack of circuit breaker.
actions_taken: Tripped circuit breaker to divert payments to secondary payment rail (Acquirer B)
Lowered upstream partner HTTP timeout from 15s to 2.5s
INC-003.resolution: Engaged circuit breaker fallback to secondary payment rail and tightened upstream timeout thresholds.
INC-003.verification: Checkout gateway latency normalized to 380ms, payment success rate recovered to 99.4%.
recommendations: Automate multi-rail active-active payment routing based on rolling p95 latency
Implement exponential backoff retry on transient gateway 504 errors
INC-003.engineer_feedback: Secondary payment rail handled 100% of volume seamlessly once circuit breaker was manually tripped.

INC-004.title: Notification Service OOMKilled Worker Pod CrashLoop
symptoms: Worker pods entering CrashLoopBackOff state repeatedly
Kubernetes container status OOMKilled (Exit Code 137)
Notification queue backlog accumulated 45,000 pending messages
investigation_steps: Retrieved pod termination events via kubectl describe pod
Analyzed JVM heap dump and native memory profiler traces
Identified unbounded byte buffer accumulation in PDF invoice attachment generator
Found unclosed file descriptors in temporary file generation routine
findings: Invoice generator was retaining unmanaged byte buffers in global scope
Each PDF attachment leaked approximately 8MB of RAM until pod exceeded 512Mi limit
INC-004.root_cause: Memory leak caused by unmanaged byte buffer retention in PDF invoice rendering library during high-volume batch dispatch.
actions_taken: Patched PDF generation logic to use streaming buffers with explicit cleanup
Temporarily bumped pod memory limit from 512Mi to 1Gi
INC-004.resolution: Updated PDF rendering buffer context disposal, enforced garbage collection, and increased pod limit to 1Gi.
INC-004.verification: Pod memory consumption stabilized at 190Mi under 10,000 notifications/min load with zero pod restarts.
recommendations: Implement container memory leak synthetic soak tests in staging pipeline
Add Prometheus alert for pod memory utilization > 80% with positive rate of change
INC-004.engineer_feedback: Memory leak hotfix verified stable across all 6 notification worker replicas.
